document_summary: This document outlines the Community Water Quality Monitoring Procedure, detailing how field teams collect and record drinking water samples for reliable and traceable results.

edits.revised: Purpose: This procedure explains how field teams collect and record drinking water samples to ensure reliable results traceable to the correct site.
edits.rationale: Revised for clarity and conciseness, maintaining the professional tone.

edits.revised: Scope: Applies to routine samples from reservoirs, treatment outlets, and public taps. Does not cover emergency chemical spills or laboratory instrument calibration.

edits.revised: Responsibilities: Team leader verifies each technician's PPE, clean sample bottles, and calibrated meter. Technicians are responsible for completing QMS-07's Chain of Custody Form and reporting unsafe conditions.
edits.rationale: The responsibilities are preserved exactly, using protected tokens. Provider label contradicted the actual source/revision difference; confirm this classification.

edits.revised: Procedure: Before sampling, allow the tap to run for 2 minutes. Rinse the probe with clean water but not sterile microbiological bottles. Record pH and turbidity in NTU at the site. Samples must be kept in a cooler between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius.
edits.rationale: Revised for clarity and technical precision, preserving all operational details.

edits.revised: Data recording: Document site code, date, time, and sampler initials on both the bottle and QMS-07. Corrections must be made with a single line through the error; correction fluids are not permitted. State the reason for any missing reading.
edits.rationale: The data recording instructions remain unchanged, maintaining technical precision. Provider label contradicted the actual source/revision difference; confirm this classification.

edits.revised: Escalation: If pH is below 6.5 or above 9.5, or turbidity is more than 1 NTU, notify the team leader immediately. Do not declare the water safe or unsafe to the community until an authorised official has reviewed the results.
